# Ninigi: the stories first, then the spelling

The marks in **Ninigi** make the most sense standing next to the myths they have to carry. So the myths come first.

## The Stories That Carry the Name

**The Descent from Heaven.** Amaterasu decided that her grandson Ninigi should rule the terrestrial world.  She gave him the Three Sacred Regalia and sent him down to Takachiho in Kyūshū.  The earthly kami Ōkuninushi initially resisted but eventually submitted after negotiations and divine pressure.

**Marriage to Konohana-Sakuya-hime.** Ninigi met the princess Konohana-Sakuya-hime, daughter of the mountain god Ōyamatsumi, beside a blossoming tree.  She promised to bear his children, but when her pregnancy was doubted, she entered a birthing hut and set it on fire, vowing that the children would survive if they were truly his.  Hoderi and Hoori were born from the flames, proving her words.

**Ancestor of Jimmu.** Through his son Hoori and grandson Ugayafukiaezu, Ninigi became the great-grandfather of Kamuyamato-Iwarebiko, later known as Emperor Jimmu.  The imperial line thus traces its ancestry directly to the sun goddess through Ninigi.

## And Here Is What the Spelling Preserves

Against those stories, the attestation: **邇邇芸命**, as Kojiki (Ninigi's descent and marriage) and Nihon Shoki (parallel descent account) record. The name means "The august rice spirit".


## At a Glance

- **Restored name:** Ninigi
- **ASCII form:** ninigi
- **Meaning:** "The august rice spirit"
- **Domain of influence:** Rice, Descendant of Amaterasu
- **Pantheon:** Japanese
- **Classification:** Tier 2
- **Original script:** 邇邇芸命
- **Series:** The Restoration Files, No. 291 of 463

## The Name Travels

Ninigi is primarily an imperial genealogical figure rather than a widely worshipped deity.  His role connects solar mythology, agricultural sovereignty, and political legitimacy.

## The Address It Earned

The temple of **Ninigi** stands at [/ninigi/](/ninigi/) — [lore](/ninigi/lore/), [scholars](/ninigi/scholars/), [patterns](/ninigi/patterns/) — because a name carrying this much story deserves more than a parking page. The restoration keeps one feature the ASCII form drops. One is enough to matter, and the label says so plainly: Tier-2.

## The Sources Are Open

The myths above are retold from the temple's record; the primary voices are in the [Sacred Texts](/texts/): [Kojiki](/texts/kojiki/) and [Nihon Shoki](/texts/nihon-shoki/). Nothing in this file outranks them.
